facility_roles.quote: The higher energy and intensity evolution of AdA, ADONE, started the study of the electron-positron collisions physics in Frascati.

intervals.label: ADONE data taking (second generation)
intervals.note: No source dates the start of the second-generation detectors. The 1974 Phys. Rev. Lett. paper (received 18 November 1974) is signed by this group and the INFN-LNF page says the second-generation detectors contributed to the J/psi measurements, so the detector was operating by November 1974; 1974 is the latest possible start and the confidence is uncertain. End: The INFN-LNF page dates the first and second generation experiments together ('from 1969 to 1978'); no source gives this experiment's own end date, so 1978 is the latest possible end and the interval is approximate.
intervals.quote: The second generation detectors at ADONE had unique features to identify some peculiar aspects of the new particle, and in this way they were able to give significant contributions to the measurement of its properties.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: The INFN-LNF page dates the first and second generation experiments together ('from 1969 to 1978'); no source gives this experiment's own end date, so 1978 is the latest possible end and the interval is approximate.
intervals.quote: The first generation experiments, and successively the second generation ones, explored the physics of electron-positron collisions up to 3.0 GeV in the center of mass, from 1969 to 1978.

intervals.label: J/psi confirmation run
intervals.locator: Phys. Rev. Lett. 33, 1408 (1974), abstract; received 18 November 1974
intervals.note: Month precision: the J/psi was announced in November 1974 and the paper was received on 18 November 1974.
intervals.quote: We report on the results at ADONE to study the properties of the newly found 3.1-BeV particle.

name: Baryon-Antibaryon (ADONE)
notes: The INFN-LNF page also lists a first-generation 'proton-antiproton' experiment of a Naples group that took the place of Boson; it does not say whether this is the same group or experiment, and none is recorded separately.

physics_goals.quote: The Baryon-Antibaryon Experiment was designed to study proton-antiproton and, more generally, any baryon-antibaryon pair, similar to protons, but with a larger mass, looking mainly at the energy threshold of the reaction.
physics_goals.value: Proton-antiproton and other baryon-antibaryon pair production in e+e- annihilation near threshold

summary.plain: A second-generation experiment at Frascati's ADONE collider that studied how electron-positron annihilation makes proton-antiproton and other baryon pairs near threshold. It took part in the 1974 study of the J/psi.
summary.technical: Baryon-Antibaryon at ADONE (second generation, operating by November 1974): large liquid scintillators, magnetostrictive wire chambers and flash tube chambers for e+e- → p p-bar and heavier baryon pairs at threshold; Frascati, Naples, Pisa and ISS; signatory of the 1974 PRL on the 3.1 GeV particle.
